content: Benznidazole is indicated for the treatment of Chagas disease (American trypanosomiasis) caused by Trypanosoma cruzi in children aged 2 to 12 years. Its safety and efficacy have not been established in children under 2 years of age. For children aged 2 to 12 years, the recommended dosage is 5 to 8 mg/kg/day, administered orally in two divided doses approximately 12 hours apart, for a duration of 60 days. The drug has not been evaluated in patients with renal or hepatic impairment. This indication has been approved under an accelerated approval process based on the number of treated patients who became negative for Immunoglobulin G (IgG) antibodies against recombinant antigens of T. cruzi. Continued approval may depend on verification and description of clinical benefits in confirmatory trials. Benznidazole is contraindicated in patients who have taken disulfiram within the last two weeks due to the risk of psychotic reactions. Co-administration of benznidazole and disulfiram increases the toxicity of both drugs through aldehyde dehydrogenase inhibition. Similarly, benznidazole increases the toxicity of ethanol via the same mechanism, and alcohol consumption during or within three days after therapy is contraindicated. Consuming alcohol or products containing propylene glycol during or after therapy with nitroimidazole agents (structurally related to benznidazole) may result in abdominal cramps, nausea, vomiting, headaches, and/or flushing. Benznidazole may interact with certain immunosuppressive therapies, such as axicabtagene ciloleucel, brexucabtagene autoleucel, ciltacabtagene autoleucel, idecabtagene vicleucel, lisocabtagene maraleucel, and tisagenlecleucel. These combinations can increase the immunosuppressive effects of both agents, leading to a higher risk of infection. It is recommended to avoid these combinations or use alternative drugs. Due to the potential for serious adverse reactions and the risk of transmitting Chagas disease, breastfeeding is not recommended during treatment with benznidazole. Benznidazole is generally considered acceptable for use during pregnancy, as controlled studies in pregnant women have shown no evidence of fetal risk. The drug is approximately 44-60% protein-bound, with an unknown metabolic pathway and a half-life of 13 hours (based on single-dose studies in healthy volunteers). It is excreted through both urine and feces. Dosage is based on body weight, and the 100-mg tablets are scored to allow precise dosing (50 mg or 25 mg). Benznidazole can be taken with or without food. It should be stored at controlled room temperature (20-25°C or 68-77°F), with permissible excursions to 15-30°C (59-86°F). The bottle should be tightly closed and protected from moisture. This information is provided for general educational purposes. Formulary status and drug coverage may vary by individual plans, and formulary information is subject to change. For the most current information, contact the applicable plan provider.
